clue.text: Unknown girl rejected god

parts.note: Z is one of the letters algebra uses for an unknown quantity

indicators.note: rejected suggests the girl's name is turned back, so it is read from right to left

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl nobody knows has spurned a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief of the Olympian deities in Greek myth, so a god by any measure.

clue.text: Where nanny voted randomly, not consistently

indicators.note: randomly tells us the letters of the preceding three words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Somebody wonders where the childminder cast her ballot, which she does only fitfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'randomly' shuffles all fifteen letters of WHERE NANNY VOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for occasionally, which is the opposite of doing something steadily or regularly.

clue.text: City girl almost climbing over car

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece on top of the next
in a down clue climbing means the letters go upwards, so they read in reverse
almost means the word loses its final letter, stopping just short

parts.note: a lass is a girl
Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: A girl in a city nearly clambers over a motor car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City girl' reads as one phrase, but City is the definition; 'almost' and 'climbing' both act on the girl, and 'over' stacks her above the car in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Salford is a city in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.

clue.text: Expose, say, rising fraud, mainly aimed at the old?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising sends both preceding pieces upwards, reversing their combined letters

parts.note: to air something is to expose it
say signals an example, abbreviated EG

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word is kept, losing its last letter

parts.note: a trick is a fraud or deception

explanation.surface: Someone exposes a growing swindle, mostly targeting pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns AIR + EG into GERIA; 'mainly' cuts TRICK to TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatric describes care or medicine for elderly people, so it is directed at the aged.

clue.text: Logic almost swayed chief member of small government

indicators.note: swayed suggests the letters are moved about into a new order
almost tells us the word drops its final letter

parts.note: arch as a prefix means chief or principal, as in archbishop

explanation.surface: Persuasive reasoning nearly won over the head of a ruling clique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts LOGIC to LOGI, and 'swayed' rearranges that into OLIG.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is rule by a small elite, and one of its ruling few is the person defined.

clue.text: Mummy's boy raised detailed thought in work

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the word for work

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially a musical composition

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters go upwards, read in reverse
detailed is read as de-tailed, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A son devoted to his mother brings up a fully worked-out idea in his composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means de-tailed: IDEA loses its tail to give IDE, which 'raised' turns to EDI. Freud's Oedipus complex is a son's attachment to his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek king who unknowingly married his mother gave his name to Freud's complex, making him the archetypal son fixated on his mother.

clue.text: Is lake reported in Turkish place?

indicators.note: reported tells us the words are spoken, so the entry is what they sound like

parts.note: is plus mere, an old word for a lake or pond

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether a stretch of water is said to be in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A mere is a lake, chiefly in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Izmir is a large port city on Turkey's Aegean coast.

clue.text: Pure fury stopped by B short sharp blow

indicators.note: by puts the next piece beside the first
stopped means the word is cut off before its end, losing its last letter

parts.note: anger is fury

indicators.note: short means the following word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lick is informally a sharp blow

explanation.surface: Blind rage is halted by a quick smack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped' cuts ANGER to ANGE and 'short' cuts LICK to LIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means saintly or innocent, which is what pure means of a person.

clue.text: Compare notes on A universal broadcast at M the same time

indicators.note: broadcast suggests the letters are scattered widely and reassembled

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Presenters swap jottings about a programme aired everywhere simultaneously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' shuffles COMPARE NOTES ON with U. The stray M on the printed page is a scanning fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemporaneous means existing or happening during the same period, simultaneous.

clue.text: Having the power to hug English tree

indicators.note: to hug means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: able means having the power or ability to do something

explanation.surface: Being strong enough to embrace an English tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar, a species of tree.

clue.text: More than half-cowardly cry

indicators.note: more than half means only the larger part of the word is kept, here four of its six letters

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly

explanation.surface: A rather timid shout.
explanation.definitionFit: To yell is to shout, a loud cry.

clue.text: Harmful obstruction, growing old

parts.note: a dam is an obstruction holding back water
aging means growing old

explanation.surface: A barrier that is getting on in years can be dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaging means causing injury or harm.

clue.text: Axes pound copra, breaking coconut?

parts.note: the axes of a graph are labelled x and y
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

indicators.note: breaking means the word's letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Somebody hacks at dried coconut meat with axes, hitting and cracking the nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges COPRA into OCARP. The question mark admits the coconut is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A xylocarp is a hard, woody fruit, and the coconut is the classic case.

clue.text: Break bottom of hull, one stuck in coral

indicators.note: stuck in means the pieces are lodged inside the next word

parts.note: a reef is often made of coral

indicators.note: bottom of picks the last letter of the following word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A ship's keel cracks when it runs aground on a coral reef.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief is a respite, a break from work or strain.

clue.text: Amazement of wife, note, ducked in European river

indicators.note: ducked in means the piece is plunged inside the river's name

parts.note: the Oder flows between Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: A wife was astonished when a message was dunked in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonder is the feeling of astonishment or awe.

clue.text: Small fly going round a painting

indicators.note: going round means the word for fly encircles the next piece

parts.note: to fly can mean to flee or escape

explanation.surface: A tiny insect buzzes around a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a painting or picture of the sea.

clue.text: Old serving women pinching young and vulnerable waiters

indicators.note: pinching means the first piece grips the second inside it

parts.note: the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army branch of the Second World War
tender can mean young and easily hurt, as in tender years

explanation.surface: Elderly waitresses nipping a delicate youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: Old crossword-style abbreviations stand for whole bodies of people: ATS was Britain's women's army in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Attenders and waiters both serve: those who wait on or attend to others.

clue.text: After farewell, name American spies leaving European city

indicators.note: after means the remaining pieces follow the word for farewell

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
the CIA is the US foreign intelligence agency

explanation.surface: After a goodbye, a named group of US agents depart from a Continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a port city on Spain's east coast.

clue.text: Two of these appear on clock given by Cockney intellectual

definitions.text: Two of these appear on clock

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the initial H, so the word is said without it

parts.note: a highbrow is an intellectual

explanation.surface: A clock face's features are drawn by an educated Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' is British slang for the face. A Londoner dropping the H says HIGHBROW as 'eyebrow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock is slang for a face, and a face has a pair of hairy arches above the eyes.

clue.text: Promote a ball around 3rd of November

indicators.note: around means the word for ball goes round the picked letter

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: 3rd of picks the third letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a winter ball at the start of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance someone is to move them forward or promote them.

clue.text: Enter pub in the smallest bit of clothing

indicators.note: enter is an instruction to put one piece into another
in names the piece that receives the other inside it

parts.note: a tad is a tiny amount
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Walking into a pub wearing next to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic, a garment once worn over armour.

clue.text: Clanger dances, happy

parts.note: balls are formal dances
up can mean cheerful, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: Joyful dances are a big mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: A clanger is British slang for a blunder; a balls-up is a cruder British word for a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a blunder or bungled job.

clue.text: Lower drinking apparatus

parts.note: read lower as one who lows, a cow, and the drinking apparatus is what her calf feeds from

explanation.definitionFit: A cow's milk-producing glands are what a calf drinks from.

clue.text: Graves through which you can see?

definitions.text: Graves through which you can see?

parts.words: Graves through which you can see?
parts.note: Graves is not burial places but a white Bordeaux wine, and pale white wine is clear enough to see through

explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a district of Bordeaux known for white wine, which is the French phrase for white wine.

clue.text: Half of what's left with one can be unlucky

annotationWithheld.why: Half of what's left with one can be unlucky (8) for THIRTEEN: 'can be unlucky' defines it, but no reading of 'Half of what's left with one' giving the letters could be found

clue.text: Lazybones left putting on blubber

indicators.note: putting on means the letter dons the word for blubber, which then wraps around it

parts.note: to blubber is to sob

explanation.surface: An idler who quit has started piling on fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A slob is a lazy, untidy person.

clue.text: Caught 4 wandering round an island

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: wandering round suggests the letters rove about into a new order

parts.note: the figure is read as the word four

explanation.surface: A catch was taken by a quartet roaming about an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 4 must be spelt out as a word before 'wandering round' can mix its letters; the C for caught is the scorecard notation in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Beetles should grip on this when it's cold

definitions.text: Beetles should grip on this when it's cold

parts.words: Beetles should grip on this when it's cold
parts.note: the beetles are not insects but Volkswagen Beetle cars, which need winter rubber for traction

explanation.definitionFit: Special winter tyres with a deep tread give cars traction on icy roads.

clue.text: Snake going round one's back, where one leans?

indicators.note: going round means the turned snake encircles the numeral
back signals the snake's name is read in reverse

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A serpent coils around somebody's spine at a place where people lean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ASP to PSA, which goes round I. Pisa's famous tower leans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city is home to the famous tilting bell tower.
